subject.title: fix(kill-tree): verify process group leader before using group kill to prevent gateway SIGTERM (#76259)

question: Should OpenClaw accept this compatibility-sensitive change where omitted `detached` Unix cleanup uses leader-verified group kill with direct-PID fallback, instead of preserving unconditional group kill for omitted callers?
rationale: Both options trade availability risks: the PR prevents gateway process-group SIGTERM for non-leaders, but changes behavior for existing omitted-option callers that expected group cleanup without explicitly passing `detached: true`.

options.title: Accept guarded default after rebase
options.body: Resolve conflicts, audit current-main callers, keep explicit `detached: true` on known detached cleanup paths, and land the leader-check/default-fallback behavior.

options.title: Require caller-state-only fix
options.body: Reject the helper default change and instead require every relevant cleanup path to carry exact spawn detachment state before changing shared behavior.

options.title: Pause for broader process-owner proof
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers get additional live macOS gateway and Linux minimal-image proof for the exact final merge result.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded default after rebase
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts, audit current-main callers, keep explicit `detached: true` on known detached cleanup paths, and land the leader-check/default-fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main process/helper movement and service-managed process history make this the best available routing signal for the compatibility decision.
